assumptions: "Total ARR" is defined as the sum of ARR from all currently in-force contracts (status = 'Activated', with start_date <= 2026-09-11 <= end_date).

The accounts.total_arr__c field was found to be unreliable/incomplete (null for many active accounts, and stored in the contract's local currency rather than USD), so ARR was computed directly from the contracts table instead.

Currency conversion to USD was done using the most recent applicable rate in dated_conversion_rates as of 2026-09-11 (USD=1.0, CAD=1.36, GBP=0.75), applying USD_amount = local_amount / conversion_rate (consistent with Salesforce's corporate-currency conversion convention).

Breakdown: USD contracts $9,322,200 (no conversion) + CAD contracts $4,147,600 / 1.36 = $3,049,706 + GBP contracts $6,808,500 / 0.75 = $9,078,000, totaling ~$21,449,906.

results.trap: departed reps still own open pipeline
assumptions: "Open pipeline" = opportunities where is_closed = false (and is_deleted = false).
"Owned by reps who are no longer active employees" = opportunities.owner_id joins to users where users.is_active = false.
ARR is taken from opportunities.arr__c.

Non-USD ARR converted to USD using dated_conversion_rates, matching the opportunity's currency_iso_code and close_date to the rate's [start_date, next_start_date) window; conversion_rate represents local-currency-per-USD, so USD amount = arr__c / conversion_rate.

One deal (id 0060129, CAD, close_date 2027-02-01) fell exactly on the boundary of the rate table's coverage with no matching window; the most recent known CAD rate (1.36, effective 2026-02-01) was applied for this deal.
15 open opportunities met the criteria, totaling ~$2,577,799 USD.
sqlQueries: select * from dated_conversion_rates limit 20;
select distinct currency_iso_code from opportunities;

select sum(o.arr__c / dcr.conversion_rate) as open_pipeline_arr_usd
from opportunities o
join users u on o.owner_id = u.id
join dated_conversion_rates dcr on dcr.iso_code = o.currency_iso_code
  and o.close_date >= dcr.start_date and o.close_date < dcr.next_start_date
where o.is_closed = false
  and u.is_active = false
  and o.is_deleted = false;

select count(*) from opportunities o
join users u on o.owner_id = u.id
left join dated_conversion_rates dcr on dcr.iso_code = o.currency_iso_code
  and o.close_date >= dcr.start_date and o.close_date < dcr.next_start_date
where o.is_closed = false and u.is_active = false and o.is_deleted = false and dcr.iso_code is null;

select o.id, o.currency_iso_code, o.close_date, o.arr__c from opportunities o
join users u on o.owner_id = u.id
left join dated_conversion_rates dcr on dcr.iso_code = o.currency_iso_code
  and o.close_date >= dcr.start_date and o.close_date < dcr.next_start_date
where o.is_closed = false and u.is_active = false and o.is_deleted = false and dcr.iso_code is null;

with rates as (
  select o.id, o.arr__c, o.currency_iso_code, o.close_date,
    coalesce(
      (select dcr.conversion_rate from dated_conversion_rates dcr
       where dcr.iso_code = o.currency_iso_code
         and o.close_date >= dcr.start_date and o.close_date < dcr.next_start_date
       limit 1),
      (select dcr.conversion_rate from dated_conversion_rates dcr
       where dcr.iso_code = o.currency_iso_code
       order by dcr.start_date desc limit 1)
    ) as rate
  from opportunities o
  join users u on o.owner_id = u.id
  where o.is_closed = false and u.is_active = false and o.is_deleted = false
)
select sum(arr__c / rate) as total_usd, count(*) from rates;

results.trap: churn definition + 60-day grace period
results.assumptions:
<parameter name="assumptions">["Churn ('logo lost') is defined as an account whose contract reached its natural end (status = 'Expired') with no subsequent (non-Cancelled) contract starting within 60 days of that end_date - i.e., the gap before any next contract exceeds 60 days, or there is no next contract at all.", "'Cancelled' contracts (all of which have future start_dates in this dataset) represent bookings/orders cancelled before ever activating, not an existing customer churning, so they were excluded from the churn count (they don't represent an active relationship ending) and were also not counted as a valid 'renewal' that would offset a gap.", "'Last 12 months' = contract end_date falling between 2025-09-11 and 2026-09-11 (today's date), since the churn event is dated by when the customer relationship actually ended.", "Counting logos means counting distinct accounts/contracts meeting the churn definition, not weighting by ARR.", "Each qualifying account had at most one Expired contract in the window, so account count = contract count (17)."]</parameter>
<parameter name="needs_clarification">false</parameter>
</invoke>
sqlQueries: SELECT status, count(*) FROM contracts GROUP BY status;
SELECT customer_status__c, count(*) FROM accounts GROUP BY customer_status__c;
SELECT account_id, id, status, start_date, end_date, arr FROM contracts ORDER BY account_id, start_date LIMIT 50;

SELECT c.account_id, c.id, c.status, c.start_date, c.end_date, c.arr
FROM contracts c
WHERE c.status IN ('Expired','Cancelled')
ORDER BY c.account_id, c.start_date;

WITH exp AS (
  SELECT c.account_id, c.id, c.end_date,
    (SELECT MIN(c2.start_date) FROM contracts c2 
       WHERE c2.account_id = c.account_id 
         AND c2.status <> 'Cancelled'
         AND c2.start_date > c.end_date) AS next_start
  FROM contracts c
  WHERE c.status = 'Expired'
    AND c.end_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-09-11' AND DATE '2026-09-11'
)
SELECT account_id, id, end_date, next_start,
  (next_start::date - end_date::date) AS gap_days,
  CASE WHEN next_start IS NULL OR (next_start::date - end_date::date) > 60 THEN 'churn' ELSE 'renewed' END AS classification
FROM exp
ORDER BY account_id;

results.trap: churn: logo count vs revenue dollars
assumptions: "Last quarter" relative to today's date (2026-09-11) is interpreted as Q2 2026: April 1 – June 30, 2026.

There is no explicit 'churn' flag/date field, so churn was defined as contracts with status='Expired' whose end_date falls in the target quarter, where the associated account's customer_status__c = 'Churned' (confirming no renewal took effect).
Any subsequent contract records found for these accounts were only in 'Draft' status (not activated), so they were not treated as renewals that would offset the churned ARR.
Churned ARR is measured as the full contract ARR (the 'arr' field on the contracts table) of the expired, non-renewed contracts.

Non-USD contract ARR (GBP, CAD) was converted to USD using the dated_conversion_rates table's rate in effect for that period (rate representing USD-to-currency, so local amount was divided by the rate).
Figure reflects gross churned ARR (logo/contract churn), not net of any expansion elsewhere, and covers 6 distinct churned customer accounts.

results.trap: 'best quarter' = new ARR, total ARR, or deal count
assumptions: "Best quarter" is measured by total closed-won ARR (arr__c) and Amount, converted to USD using the dated_conversion_rates table, for opportunities closed in calendar year 2026 (year-to-date through 2026-09-11).
Quarters follow standard calendar quarters (Q1=Jan-Mar, Q2=Apr-Jun, Q3=Jul-Sep, Q4=Oct-Dec).
Q3 2026 is only partially complete (through Sep 11) as of today's date, so its total is naturally lower and was compared as-is (not annualized/prorated).

Q2 2026 had the highest closed-won Amount (~$5.10M USD) and ARR (~$4.46M USD) with 34 won deals, edging out Q1 2026 (~$4.90M Amount / $3.52M ARR, 34 deals) and well ahead of the partial Q3 2026 (~$2.01M / $2.01M, 20 deals).
sqlQueries: SELECT currency_iso_code, count(*) FROM opportunities GROUP BY 1

SELECT date_trunc('quarter', close_date) AS q, count(*), sum(amount) AS sum_amount, sum(arr__c) AS sum_arr
FROM opportunities
WHERE is_won = true AND is_closed = true AND close_date >= '2026-01-01' AND close_date <= '2026-09-11'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT date_trunc('quarter', o.close_date) AS q,
       count(*) AS deals,
       sum(o.amount / COALESCE(cr.conversion_rate,1)) AS amount_usd,
       sum(o.arr__c / COALESCE(cr.conversion_rate,1)) AS arr_usd
FROM opportunities o
LEFT JOIN dated_conversion_rates cr
  ON cr.iso_code = o.currency_iso_code
  AND o.close_date >= cr.start_date
  AND (o.close_date < cr.next_start_date OR cr.next_start_date IS NULL)
WHERE o.is_won = true AND o.is_closed = true
  AND o.close_date >= '2026-01-01' AND o.close_date <= '2026-09-11'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
